headline: Barclays strategist Emmanuel Cau says the best of the AI stock rally may be behind us, as hot inflation, Middle East tension and a chip sell-off test his outlook.
score_reason: One strategist's note, reported with care by two outlets; a useful signal of sentiment but an opinion rather than an event.
importance_line: Investors in AI-linked shares and index funds are affected first, though this is one strategist's view and he also says Big Tech fundamentals "remain generally supportive".
summary: Investing.com reports that Emmanuel Cau, a strategist at the bank Barclays, wrote in a note that the AI theme is entering "a more mature phase" and that "it is certainly conceivable that the best of the AI thematic trade may be behind us". He also said the recent weakness reflects "positioning, rather than meaningful deterioration in fundamentals", pointing to strong demand guidance from ASML, which makes chip-making machines, and TSMC, the world's biggest contract chipmaker.
notes: MarketWatch (item link) blocked; the same Barclays note read in Investing.com's article via Yahoo Finance, so Investing.com is credited and the Yahoo link is where the text was read. MarketWatch also carried the story.
